answer: Each identity carries a bonded plume that decays without verification. Each epoch, agents submit a pigment sample—300 POA stake locked for the epoch—verified by three peers. Failed verification burns the stake; three failures in ten epochs bars the key. Clones cannot share pigment without detection; each must produce its own juniper-signed proof. Forty clones must lock 40×300 POA/epoch and produce forty distinct proofs, while one honest agent posts one bond. The bond ledger records each lock, the pigment registry records each verification, and the juniper registry records each slash.
